claim: GrapheneOS lists official production support for 21 devices: Pixel 6/6 Pro/6a, 7/7 Pro/7a, Pixel Fold, Pixel Tablet (tangorpro), 8/8 Pro/8a, 9/9 Pro/9 Pro XL/9 Pro Fold/9a and 10/10 Pro/10 Pro XL/10 Pro Fold/10a

GrapheneOS recommends buying only Pixel 8 or later (8/8 Pro/8a through 10a); 8th-generation and later Pixels have a 7-year minimum support guarantee and hardware memory tagging (MTE), which GrapheneOS uses by default for the base OS and known-compatible apps with an opt-in for all apps

GrapheneOS FAQ table of OEM minimum support end: Pixel 6/6 Pro Oct 2026; Pixel 6a Jul 2027; Pixel 7/7 Pro Oct 2027; Pixel 7a May 2028; Pixel Tablet Jun 2028 (5 years); Pixel 8/8 Pro Oct 2030; Pixel 8a May 2031; Pixel 9 family Aug 2031; Pixel 9a Apr 2032; Pixel 10/10 Pro/10 Pro XL Aug 2032; Pixel 10 Pro Fold Oct 2032; Pixel 10a Mar 2033. Official updates typically end shortly after.
GrapheneOS FAQ: devices sold in partnership with carriers may be carrier-locked, which prevents installing GrapheneOS; primarily an issue with US carriers

GrapheneOS per-app 'Exploit protection compatibility mode' switches the app from hardened_malloc to Android's Scudo allocator, reduces address space from 48-bit to 39-bit, disables memory tagging unless the app opted in, and allows ptrace; each change can also be toggled separately

GrapheneOS crash reporting tells users when hardened_malloc or hardware memory tagging caught memory corruption, and lets them choose whether to enable compatibility toggles; the usage guide asks for a 'Take bug report' capture (tombstones) plus an OS issue-tracker report for aborting apps

On GrapheneOS, sandboxed Google Play is a regular app installed per user/work profile with no special access; by default location requests from Play-dependent apps are rerouted to GrapheneOS's own reimplementation of the Play geolocation service, so no permission needs to be granted to Play services

GrapheneOS network location is opt-in (Settings > Location > Location services > Network location) using Apple's service or a GrapheneOS proxy to it; Wi-Fi and Bluetooth scanning are disabled by default; position data is cached in memory up to 15 minutes so it works briefly offline

GrapheneOS extends Android's eBPF filtering to block apps sending multicast outside the VPN tunnel and adds a netfilter multicast firewall that only permits multicast on interfaces the process may use

GrapheneOS issue #8066 (open since 2026-06-22): multicast over a ZeroTier VPN does not work on a GrapheneOS Pixel 9a while the same setup on stock Pixel 9a lets ATAK devices see each other; a later comment says it affects all multicast over VPN interfaces [user reports; not a maintainer statement]

Google's Pixel Tablet spec page lists Tensor G2, Titan M2, 8 GB RAM, Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.2, UWB and Google Cast under 'Connectivity and location', and sensors without a GNSS receiver or barometer: the tablet has no satellite positioning and no cellular modem

GrapheneOS 2024111700 release notes: 'fix Mock Location on devices without any standard location providers (only Pixel Tablet)' and 'temporarily disable hardened_malloc for vendor audio service due to Pixel Tablet bug'
GrapheneOS issue #6727 (open since 2025-12-09): Pixel Tablet soft-reboots (system crash, DeadSystemException) when switching user profiles since release 2025112101

GrapheneOS issue #4306 (closed 2024-11-15): on Pixel Tablet the vendor audio HAL crashed with SIGSEGV inside vendor libedgetpu_util/libspeechenhancer when starting calls; this matches the hardened_malloc exemption for the vendor audio service in 2024111700

ATAK-CIV 5.5.1.10 InternalGPSLocationProvider requests LocationManager.GPS_PROVIDER and catches IllegalArgumentException ('location updates are not available on this device') with a hint dialog instead of crashing; NetworkLocationProvider does the same for NETWORK_PROVIDER

ATAK-CIV build: default 'civ' flavor packages armeabi-v7a, arm64-v8a, x86 and x86_64 native code; the Play-store 'civSmall' flavor and others package arm64-v8a only; targetSdkVersion 35, minSdkVersion 21 (24 for firstnetSmall)
GrapheneOS 2024062700 fully removed 32-bit ARM support on Pixel 7/7 Pro/7a, Pixel Tablet and Pixel Fold; 2024071200 temporarily re-allowed the 32-bit syscall ABI for buggy anti-tampering libraries

No public report of ATAK crashing on a GrapheneOS Pixel Tablet was found: the GrapheneOS os-issue-tracker search for 'ATAK' returns only #8066 (multicast), the TAK-Product-Center/atak-civ tracker has no GrapheneOS or tablet crash issue, and web searches found none [method claim, searches run 2026-11-11]

Constellation Response (2024-10-25): with ATAK on a GrapheneOS phone and a stock Samsung, the GrapheneOS phone saw the Samsung's position but the Samsung did not see the GrapheneOS phone; editing the Meshtastic ATAK plugin hop limit on GrapheneOS broke the plugin; MAC randomization repeatedly tripped a Wi-Fi allowlist; the author recommends a stock Samsung instead [single blog, not reproduced]
GoTAK sells the 'EUD V3', a Pixel 9 with GrapheneOS and a preloaded ATAK/TAK plugin stack, carrier-unlocked, listed at USD 1,500 (out of stock on 2026-11-11) [vendor marketing]

Samsung Knox Warranty Bit is a one-time hardware e-fuse set when Trusted Boot detects an unsigned kernel or a disabled security feature such as SELinux; once set, device-bound KeyStore data becomes inaccessible and Knox functions (e.g. creating a work profile) and Knox-dependent services (e.g. Samsung Pay) may stop working, regardless of later actions

US Snapdragon Galaxy models (U/U1) have no OEM-unlocking option, and in July 2025 One UI 8 builds were reported to remove the OEM-unlocking toggle on global models too [press analysis of firmware; no official Samsung statement found]
component: Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra / One UI 8

claim: Shizuku (lets apps use ADB-level system APIs without root) is Apache-2.0; its GitHub repo was last pushed 2025-06-18
Universal Android Debloater Next Generation is GPL-3.0 and active (last push 2026-11-05)
Obtainium (installs and updates APKs directly from source releases) is GPL-3.0 and active (last push 2026-11-01)
Shelter (isolates apps in an Android work profile) is GPL-3.0; its GitHub repo was last pushed 2026-09-27

CalyxOS 8.0.5.20 (2026-11-03) is available for Fairphone Gen. 6, Fairphone 5 and 4, several moto g models and Pixel 6 through 10a including Pixel Tablet; the Android 17 rollout began 2026-10-01; Verizon Pixels cannot install it; CalyxOS should run with a relocked bootloader
/e/OS documentation lists an official Android 16 (A16) build for The Fairphone (Gen. 6/Gen. 6+), codename FP6

postmarketOS renamed itself Nura (announced 2026-09-27; postmarketos.org now redirects to nura.eco); it is based on Alpine Linux with mainline kernels; last stable release v26.06 'Alpen Avocado' (2026-06-21); the project says it is 'not yet ready for everyone'

FuriLabs FLX1s runs FuriOS (Linux) on a MediaTek Dimensity 900 with 8 GB RAM, 5,000 mAh battery, microSD and hardware switches for microphone, camera and modem/GPS; listed at USD 499 (sale) and out of stock on 2026-11-11 [vendor page]
Waydroid (GPL-3.0) has no built-in GPS pass-through: issue #226 'pass location/gps info to waydroid' has been open since 2021-11-13 with 91 comments of user workarounds
The Ubuntu Touch device site lists 111 supported devices and warns that some ports are not recently updated

GrapheneOS 2025030900 added the experimental Android 15 QPR2 virtual machine management app (Terminal: one Debian VM via a WebView terminal, developer options only); later releases backported tabs, port forwarding and GUI with opt-in GPU acceleration (VirGL), and 2026011000 fixed its use in secondary-user Private Space

Android lock task mode runs allowlisted apps kiosk-style; only apps allowlisted by a device policy controller (DPC) can run in it; available from Android 5.0 on fully managed devices and Android 9 on secondary users
Headwind MDM server and Android agent are Apache-2.0 and active (server last push 2026-11-06, agent 2026-10-20); the vendor advertises QR enrollment and air-gapped operation

OpenHarmony DSoftBus is Apache-2.0 and provides device discovery, connection, networking/topology and message/byte/stream/file transmission over WLAN and Bluetooth for near-field devices (GitHub mirror of the Gitee repo)

HarmonyOS NEXT (HarmonyOS 5 and later) removed AOSP and the Android runtime, so it cannot run Android APKs; Huawei was reported in Aug 2026 to have passed 100,000 native apps [secondary reports; counts inconsistent across sources]
iTAK on the Apple App Store requires iOS 17 or later and states compatibility with TAK Server, WinTAK, ATAK and WebTAK
Volla sells the Volla Phone Quintus and Plinius with a choice of Volla OS or Ubuntu Touch [vendor page]
The GrapheneOS releases page lists 80 release tags in 2025 and 50 in 2026 up to 2026110800 (several per month), each covering every supported Pixel

GrapheneOS states it plans to partner with OEMs to produce devices meeting its requirements, and that future devices need at least 5 years of updates for phones and 7 for tablets, MTE, pKVM and secure-element features
